answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post bids or claim rewards. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake agent separately, so splitting one actor into a hundred names multiplies the capital tied up; if identities are caught coordinating to claim the same task, the protocol can slash their deposits. The stake acts as an anchor, not proof of unique personhood, and the cost is real: capital is immobilized and exposed to loss. A harbor or knoll can name a task venue, but neither makes fake identities free.
